mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in PARKS mobility acts as a broad outing signal that carries into nearby retail trips within one to two weeks. If outdoor activity keeps rising, RETAIL_REC should improve relative to the last four weeks because leisure excursions convert into shopping and dining stops.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -30.9 to -10.1 over four weeks while RETAIL_REC improved from -11.7 to -8.4
failure_condition: If PARKS continues to rise over the next two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not become higher than its last-28-day mean, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in WORKPLACES mobility raises weekday corridor traffic and lunch-time shopping demand, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. This signal is strongest when WORKPLACES is rising on a weekly basis rather than merely fluctuating.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises week-on-week for at least 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES is still below baseline but has shown a recent improvement pattern before the latest dip
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES posts two consecutive weekly increases and RETAIL_REC is still not higher over the next 28 days than over the prior 28 days, the claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility stays elevated while TRANSIT remains deeply depressed, people shift toward local errands and neighborhood retail rather than long trips, supporting RETAIL_REC within one week. The effect depends on home-centered substitution rather than commuting recovery.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -25 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +4
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is 5.7 at t-0w while TRANSIT is -31.0
failure_condition: If the residential-high/transit-low pattern persists for a week and RETAIL_REC does not rise above its recent four-week average, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp recovery in TRANSIT mobility signals easing movement frictions and wider willingness to make discretionary trips. Once TRANSIT moves materially upward from its current depressed level, retail and recreation should follow with a short lag over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points week-on-week from a base below -30
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is approximately flat near -31.0 across the snapshot
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rises by 3 or more points from a below -30 base and RETAIL_REC does not improve within two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A continuing rise in PARKS combined with stable GROCERY_PHARM indicates stronger weekend and household activity, which spills into retail visits over the next four weeks. The effect should be positive only when both leisure and routine errands are firm at the same time.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved strongly from -30.9 to -10.1 while GROCERY_PHARM stayed positive
failure_condition: If PARKS keeps strengthening while GROCERY_PHARM remains positive and RETAIL_REC is still lower over the next 28 days, the interaction claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: The recent drop in WORKPLACES after a brief improvement indicates fewer commute-linked shopping opportunities, which should weigh on RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks. The signal is downward because commuting intensity is the main conduit for incidental retail spending.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls by 5 points or more from the prior week after a short rise
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -10.6 to -21.0 in the latest week
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES drops sharply but RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the previous two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both recover together, retail activity should rise because the combined return of commuting and public movement restores downtown foot traffic. The effect should appear within four weeks and will be stronger than either series alone.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both turn upward for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both series are currently deeply negative, with TRANSIT near -31 and WORKPLACES near -21 at t-0w
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES trend upward for two weeks and RETAIL_REC still does not exceed its last-28-day mean, the mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A stabilization in GROCERY_PHARM above zero while PARKS stays near baseline marks a normalized household routine that shifts some discretionary spending back to retail. This effect is conditional on neither proxy showing a renewed drop.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 0 and PARKS rises to at least -5
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is positive throughout the snapshot while PARKS improved sharply by t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays above zero and PARKS gets near baseline but RETAIL_REC does not improve within one week, the hypothesis is rejected.
